raw_response:
I've been working this land for thirty years, so I don't need to think too hard about the basics — my hands know what to do. But let me think through each crop carefully.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant on the 15 mu after October 10th, same as always. I use the Hebei-adapted improved variety the seed station sells — not the most expensive hybrid, but reliable. I'll rotary-till right after the maize comes off in September. Nitrogen I put down in two applications: base dressing and then topdress at jointing. I've been doing about 18 kg N/mu — maybe a little heavy, but I've never had a bad yield from it. Four irrigations: sowing water, pre-winter freezing, jointing stage, heading. That's the Quzhou way with our wells. Two pesticide sprays — one for rust and aphids before heading.

**Maize (summer):** Same 15 mu, goes in right after wheat harvest in June. No time to waste, I direct seed into the stubble. I've switched to郑单958 hybrid, good standby. Summer rains usually carry us, so I only irrigate once or twice if July turns dry. I apply all the nitrogen I need — split: some at sowing with the phosphorus, rest at big flare.

**Chrysanthemum:** I keep 5 mu for chrysanthemum. It's our cash crop, my wife and daughters handle most of the labor since my sons work in the city. I propagate from cuttings saved from last year's plants — no need to buy new every year. It needs more attention: deeper ploughing, more water, and I spray three times for aphids and powdery mildew. We sell dried flowers to the local buyer in November.

With some family off-farm, I keep the chrysanthemum area at 5 mu — it's enough for the labor we have at home.
